title: Directed union of finite etale subalgebras of an arbitrary field algebra
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $A$ a commutative unital $k$-algebra, allowing the zero algebra. Let $\mathcal E_k(A)$ be the set of unital $k$-subalgebras $D\subseteq A$ for which $\operatorname{Spec}D\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is finite and etale [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism]. This set is nonempty and directed under inclusion. Its set-theoretic union $B_k(A)=\bigcup_{D\in\mathcal E_k(A)}D$ is a $k$-subalgebra of $A$, and every finite subset of $B_k(A)$ is contained in some $D\in\mathcal E_k(A)$. Every idempotent $e\in A$, meaning $e^2=e$, belongs to $B_k(A)$. For every finite etale $k$-algebra $C$ and every unital $k$-algebra map $h:C\to A$, the image $h(C)$ belongs to $\mathcal E_k(A)$; in particular $h$ factors uniquely through the inclusion $B_k(A)\subseteq A$.

source.place: Tags 0CKR (lemma-class-weakly-etale-over-field), 0CKS (lemma-max-weakly-etale-subalgebra), and 0CKT (lemma-properties-of-max-weakly-etale-subalgebra): the finite-subalgebra union description; see also Milne Proposition 1.29, preliminary paragraph.

proof.text: First prove the image assertion, for any finite etale $k$-algebra $C$ and map $h:C\to A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-over-field-product], write $C=\prod_{i=1}^nL_i$ with each $L_i/k$ finite separable. Let $I=\ker h$ and let $e_i$ be the coordinate idempotents. If $x\in I$ has $x_i\ne0$, multiply $x$ by the tuple supported at $i$ with value $x_i^{-1}$; this gives $e_i\in I$. Thus, for $J=\{i:e_i\notin I\}$, $I$ consists exactly of tuples vanishing on $J$: the reverse inclusion follows by expressing such a tuple as the finite sum of its coordinates times the $e_i\in I$. Consequently $h(c)\mapsto(c_i)_{i\in J}$ is a well-defined algebra isomorphism $h(C)\simeq\prod_{i\in J}L_i$: injectivity follows from the description of $I$, and surjectivity by extending a tuple by zeros. Each factor is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-extension-etale], and the product is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-finite-product]. It is a finite $k$-module: combine finite spanning families of its factors. The affine definition [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] therefore makes its spectrum finite over $k$. This proves $h(C)\in\mathcal E_k(A)$, including $J=\varnothing$, whose product is the zero algebra.

source.place: Tag 0CKR, lemma-class-weakly-etale-over-field, proof of (5), the finite-product quotient argument; algebra.tex Tag 00U3, lemma-etale-over-field

proof.text: The identity extension $k/k$ is finite separable (every element has the linear minimal polynomial $T-a$), hence etale by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-extension-etale] and finite by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Apply step 1 to the structure map $k\to A$. Its image is in $\mathcal E_k(A)$, proving nonemptiness even when $A=0$.

For $D,E\in\mathcal E_k(A)$ form $T=D\otimes_kE$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-base-change], $\operatorname{Spec}T\to\operatorname{Spec}D$ is etale, and by clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] its composite to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is etale. If $(d_i)$ and $(e_j)$ are finite spanning families for $D,E$, the tensors $d_i\otimes e_j$ span $T$: expand each pure tensor bilinearly, and every tensor is a finite sum of pure tensors. Thus $T$ is finite over $k$ by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Multiplication in $A$ defines the algebra map $\mu:T\to A$, $d\otimes e\mapsto de$; the formula is balanced and multiplicative because $A$ is commutative. Step 1 gives $F=\mu(T)\in\mathcal E_k(A)$. Since $\mu(d\otimes1)=d$ and $\mu(1\otimes e)=e$, $F$ contains both $D$ and $E$, proving directedness.

source.place: Tag 0CKS, lemma-max-weakly-etale-subalgebra, first two sentences of proof; finite-stage version

proof.text: Put $B=\bigcup_{D\in\mathcal E_k(A)}D$. Nonemptiness gives a member containing $0$, $1$, and every scalar. If $x,y\in B$, choose members containing them and a common upper bound from step 3; it contains $x+y$, $xy$, and $-x$. Hence $B$ is a unital $k$-subalgebra of $A$.

For a finite subset $S\subseteq B$, induct on its cardinality. For $S=\varnothing$ use the member of step 2. Given a member containing $S$ and $x\in B$, choose a member containing $x$ and then a common upper bound by step 3. It contains $S\cup\{x\}$. This proves the finite-subset assertion.

source.place: Tag 0CKS, lemma-max-weakly-etale-subalgebra, finite subsets of the directed union

proof.text: For an idempotent $e\in A$, the algebra $k\times k$ is finite etale: apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-extension-etale] to $k/k$, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-finite-product] to its two copies, and [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] to the spanning family $(1,0),(0,1)$. The formula $h_e(a,b)=ae+b(1-e)$ gives a unital $k$-algebra map since $e(1-e)=0$ and $e+(1-e)=1$. Step 1 puts its image in $\mathcal E_k(A)$, and $h_e(1,0)=e$, so $e\in B$. Finally, for any $h:C\to A$ as in step 1, its image lies in $B$. Sending $c$ to the same value $h(c)$ regarded in $B$ is the required factorization; all algebra identities are inherited from $A$. Two factorizations agree pointwise because $B\hookrightarrow A$ is injective.
